This highlights Tether’s banking access problem, relying on smaller offshore banks and payment middlemen to reach the dollar system.

📌 Reentrancy: How a Smart Contract Can Open the Door to an Attack

Main Points
⏺ Reentrancy happens when a contract gives control to an external contract too early
⏺ An attacker can call the function again before balances are updated
⏺ This post explains why execution order can decide the safety of funds

1️⃣ Core Idea — a contract sends funds or calls another contract, and that contract jumps back into the original function.
2️⃣ The Problem — if the user balance is reduced after sending funds, the attacker may withdraw multiple times.
3️⃣ Why It’s Dangerous — the contract “thinks” funds are still available even though withdrawal already started.
4️⃣ Common Defense — update state first, send funds after, and use protective locks.
5️⃣ Practical Check — if a protocol handles withdrawals, external calls, and complex logic, audits matter a lot.

Final Thoughts

Reentrancy is an attack on execution order. Sometimes the bug is not what the contract does, but when it does it.

The Real Gold Rush: Expanding the Surface

You were duped. Again. 

We all saw the “massive” walkout from the UN general assembly. It seemed like Bibi was talking to en empty room. Some journalists even reported that. Even some Israeli journalists made that claim. 

Guess what. The media lied to you. Shocked?

Here are the facts. 

The footage is real. As Netanyahu walked up to speak, dozens of diplomats got up and left. It looks like most of the world refused to listen to him. Some even called it proof that Israel is now a pariah state. 

And now, reality. 

More than 120 countries stayed. That's nearly two-thirds of the world. 

All five veto powers stayed: the U.S., China, Britain and France. 

So did most of Europe. Even Ireland, one of Israel's toughest critics remained. 

So who walked out? And why does it look like so many? 

Each country gets six seats in this hall, so when one delegation walks out, several people stand up and walk. 

And the Palestinian mission had asked countries to bring as many staff as possible and walk out together. 

That can make a walkout bigger than the number of countries behind it. 

In Europe, Spain was the only major country to leave its seat empty. 

In Latin America, Brazil walked out. 

South Africa's seats were empty too. 

The rest were mostly small Caribbean island nations, which skip most speeches anyway. 

Even in the Muslim world, at least two countries, UAE and Bahrain, stayed. 

The walkout was real, but most of the world stayed in the room.

Just thought you’d wanna know the truth.
